Researchers examined 244 nodules and found more than 4,100 animals living in their cracks and cavities, including unique communities unlike those in the surrounding seafloor mud. These remarkable miniature habitats could now be threatened by deep-sea mining for valuable metals.

title: The secret to building Moon bases may be hiding in emergency blankets
summary: Scientists have turned the thin plastic used in emergency blankets into remarkably strong insulation that could help astronauts survive the Moon's extreme temperatures. Built from hundreds of stacked layers, the material withstands crushing pressure without losing its thermal protection, potentially paving the way for tougher, longer-lasting lunar habitats.

title: Physicists defy expectations by controlling the magnetic heart of a single atom
summary: Scientists have unexpectedly discovered how to control the magnetic spin inside a single atom's nucleus using radio waves, overturning previous assumptions about atomic behavior. The breakthrough could pave the way for more reliable quantum memory, although researchers are still trying to understand why it works.

title: An ancient virus may help explain what makes the human brain different
summary: A virus that infected chimpanzees millions of years ago may have helped shape one of the most important differences between humans and our closest relatives: how our brains develop. Scientists at Lund University discovered that ancient viral DNA embedded in the chimpanzee genome switches off a gene called LINC00662, which remains active in humans and appears to play an important role in early brain development.

title: Vitamin C could help block cancer-linked chemicals in your stomach, study finds
summary: Scientists have discovered that vitamin C may help prevent potentially cancer-causing chemicals from forming in the stomach after eating foods containing nitrates and nitrites. A new mathematical model suggests that taking vitamin C after meals could reduce these harmful reactions, offering a possible new strategy for lowering cancer risk.

title: A common osteoporosis drug blocked spinal damage in a surprising new study
summary: Scientists have uncovered a surprising genetic connection to spinal degeneration and found that an existing osteoporosis drug can prevent damaging mineral buildup in zebrafish spines. The discovery could pave the way for new treatments that slow or prevent a major cause of chronic back pain.

title: Uranus and Neptune’s bizarre magnetic fields may finally be explained
summary: The strange, wildly tilted magnetic fields of Uranus and Neptune have puzzled scientists since NASA's Voyager 2 spacecraft explored the planets in the 1980s. New simulations suggest that extreme conditions deep inside these icy giants create unusual electrical properties that could explain their magnetic fields. Remarkably, the models indicate that their magnetic poles could shift by tens of degrees within just a few decades, far faster than Earth's.

title: Astronomers discover a dead star spinning every 8 minutes and sending mysterious radio pulses
summary: Scientists have discovered a strange stellar pair more than 5,000 light-years away, where a dead star spinning every eight minutes produces mysterious radio pulses while orbiting a Sun-like star. The breakthrough also revealed massive magnetic storms on the companion star, offering fresh clues to one of astronomy's emerging mysteries.

title: A simple supplement could help your immune system fight cancer and viral infections
summary: A surprising discovery from Rockefeller University suggests that a common amino acid could play a powerful role in protecting against cancer and viral infections. Scientists found that low arginine levels interfere with the immune system's ability to recognize dangerous cells, while increasing arginine intake reduced colon cancer tumors and improved viral infection outcomes in mice. Even more remarkably, giving mice arginine after they contracted influenza helped them recover.

title: Alzheimer’s may start shrinking two brain regions years before memory loss
summary: Johns Hopkins scientists have uncovered hidden warning signs of Alzheimer’s disease that may appear up to a decade before memory loss begins. Brain scans revealed that two regions involved in memory and emotion start shrinking before the hippocampus, the area doctors typically examine for signs of Alzheimer’s. These early changes are linked to abnormal tau protein buildup and could provide a powerful new way to identify people at risk.

title: Scientists discover a bizarre paradox among endangered penguins
summary: A groundbreaking drone survey has revealed a startling split in the fate of New Zealand's endangered Erect-crested penguins. While one population has remained stable for decades, another has declined by more than 40%, apparently due to a combination of predators, worsening storms, and changing ocean conditions. Even more surprisingly, the tiny Bounty Islands support nearly as many breeding pairs as the Antipodes Islands, despite being 40 times smaller.

title: Dinosaurs may have been eating seaweed 100 million years ago
summary: Dinosaurs may have been snacking on seaweed and other ocean foods more than 100 million years ago, according to surprising new evidence hidden in their fossilized teeth. Researchers discovered chemical signatures suggesting that coastal dinosaurs and other prehistoric animals relied partly on nutrients originating in the sea. The findings reveal that marine resources traveled through ancient food chains, supplementing the diets of everything from plant-eating dinosaurs to predators.

title: Physicists use laser light to unlock a crystal's hidden electrical powers
summary: Scientists have discovered how to use flashes of laser light to organize tiny electrical regions inside a crystal, solving a decades-old mystery about how the material behaves. The laser-induced alignment lasts just a trillionth of a second, but the breakthrough could open the door to new ways of processing and storing information.

title: Euclid discovers ancient cosmic beacons from the dawn of time, shining like a trillion suns
summary: ESA’s Euclid space telescope has discovered 31 ancient quasars, including two record-breaking objects that shone with the brightness of a trillion Suns when the Universe was just 670 million years old. Powered by supermassive black holes, these extraordinary cosmic beacons reveal a time when the first galaxies were still taking shape.

title: Scientists find a simple daily routine linked to less pain and depression
summary: A simple change to your daily routine could make a surprising difference in how you feel, both physically and mentally. University of Missouri researchers found that older adults who followed consistent daily schedules reported less physical pain and fewer symptoms of depression, even when they struggled with insomnia. Keeping regular times for sleeping, eating, and other activities may help regulate the body's internal clock, which influences mood, sleep, and overall health.
